div.p: What HE said to his heart in the war camp.

lg.l: akaliru vicumpakam putaiyap pāayp
pakaluṭaṉ karanta palkatir vāṉa
miruṅkaḷiṟ ṟiṉanirai kuḷirppa vīcip
perumpeya la[ḻi]tuḷi poḻita lāṉātu
vēntaṉum vempakai muraṇi yēntilai
viṭukatir neṭuvē limaikkum pācaṟai
yaṭupukaḻ mēvaloṭu kaṇpaṭai yilaṉē
yamaru namvayi ṉatuvē namareṉ
ṉammaṟivu teḷitta pomma lōti
yāṅkā kuvaḷko ṟāṉē yōṅkuviṭaip
paṭucuva[ṟ] koṇṭa pakuvāyt teṇmaṇi
yāpeyar kōvala rāmpalō ṭaḷaiip
paiyu ṇalyāḻ cevvaḻi vakuppa
vāruyi raṇaṅkun teḷḷicai
māri mālaiyun tamiyaḷ kēṭṭē.
The flow of dwindling droplets from the great rain does not end,
pouring coolly from herds of dark bull elephants
in the many-rayed sky that is hidden along with the day,
spread for the wide dark vault of heaven to be covered,
and the king, in [his] wish for murderous fame, does not close [his] eyes,
in the encampment winking with ray-emitting long spears
with eminent leaf [tips], having encountered hot enmity.
How will she be, [she with] thick hair,
to whom our understanding has been made clear:
“[these are] our people. That [means] war too is upon us.”
– hearing alone all evening the showers
of clear sound that torment [her] precious life,
when the sorrowful good lute is assigned to a Cevvaḻi [melody],
mingling with the lily [flute] of the cowherds coming back from the cows,
[and] the gaping clear bells worn on the moving napes of tall bulls?
hearing alone all through the rainy evening
the clear sound that torments [her] precious life
